security_audit.summary: The review confirms legitimate but risky DevOps capabilities: Azure CLI, azd, PowerShell, shell execution, environment handling, Azure API calls, and local file writes. The critical static hits for jailbreak terms and Azure credential directories are false positives because they document guardrails or configuration paths rather than malicious prompt injection or credential theft. No separate semantic prompt injection, social engineering, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Command execution can affect local machines and Azure subscriptions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before az, azd, shell, or PowerShell commands, and show the target subscription, resource group, and environment.

remediation.issue: Several workflows handle API keys, Azure credential environment variables, .env files, and azd environment values.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity and project connections, redact secrets from logs, and avoid copying secret values into metadata or prompts.

remediation.issue: The grader calibration script executes local grader source with exec and compile.
remediation.suggestion: Replace dynamic execution with a constrained grader interface, or require a trusted local path and a clear warning before execution.

remediation.issue: Dataset, evaluation, and training scripts write local files and temporary artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain writes to the selected project or .foundry output folders, and ask before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Network requests target Azure APIs and Foundry endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Keep endpoints scoped to expected Microsoft Azure domains, use timeouts, and present the target resource before mutating requests.

content.value_statement: Foundry agent projects require coordinated setup across azd, Azure resources, models, tools, and evaluations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through those workflows with project-specific checks and handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Route Foundry requests to focused sub-skills for create, deploy, invoke, observe, trace, troubleshoot, and routine workflows.
Guide hosted agent scaffolding and deployment with Azure Developer CLI and Foundry project context.
Support evaluation setup, batch runs, continuous evaluation, prompt optimization, trace analysis, and dataset curation.
Assist model deployment planning across presets, custom settings, capacity, quota, and region choices.
Provide fine-tuning guidance for SFT, DPO, RFT, graders, training data, checkpoints, and deployment.
Handle RBAC, project creation, resource creation, private networking, and connection setup guidance.
limitations: It does not replace Azure portal permissions, billing, quota approvals, or organization policy decisions.
Many workflows require Azure CLI, azd, extensions, local project files, and authenticated user context.
It can propose and run commands only when the host tool permits command execution.
It should not be used for general Azure deployment outside Foundry-focused workflows.

use_cases.title: Create a Hosted Agent
use_cases.description: Scaffold a hosted Foundry agent, connect it to a project, deploy it, and run a smoke test.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Quality
use_cases.description: Build evaluation datasets, run batch evaluations, inspect traces, and optimize prompts or instructions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Plan resources, model capacity, quota, RBAC, networking, and deployment settings for Foundry workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Foundry Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new Azure AI Foundry project for a hosted agent. Ask for any missing subscription, region, and project details first.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Hosted Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Foundry agent project, verify the azd environment, and guide me through a safe deployment and smoke test.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Agent Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up an evaluation workflow for my Foundry agent, suggest datasets and evaluators, then help analyze failures and optimize instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production readiness plan for a Foundry agent, including RBAC, quota, model capacity, private networking, evaluation, and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: Create a new hosted Foundry agent from scratch.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the quick-start create workflow, checks required Azure and azd context, asks for missing project choices, and outlines the deployment path.

output_examples.input: Evaluate my deployed support agent and improve the prompt.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the observe workflow, prepares evaluation setup, recommends dataset and evaluator checks, and summarizes optimization actions for review.

output_examples.input: Find a region with capacity for a model deployment.
output_examples.output: The skill routes to model capacity guidance, compares available regions and quotas, and explains deployment tradeoffs before any Azure changes.

best_practices: Confirm the target subscription, resource group, project endpoint, agent root, and environment before write operations.
Prefer managed identity and project connections over raw API keys when a workflow supports both.
Keep generated evaluation artifacts under the selected .foundry folder and review them before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not run deployment, quota, RBAC, or cleanup commands against an inferred subscription.
Do not paste secrets into prompts when managed identity, environment variables, or project connections can be used.
Do not reuse stale azd environment values across development, staging, and production projects.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: It can guide resource creation workflows. Actual creation depends on available tools, permissions, and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can it manage existing Foundry agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports deployment, invocation, observation, tracing, troubleshooting, routines, and evaluation workflows for existing agents.

faq.question: Does it require Azure CLI or azd?
faq.answer: Most hands-on workflows require Azure CLI, Azure Developer CLI, related extensions, and an authenticated Azure context.

faq.question: Can it help with model deployment capacity?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes model deployment routing for preset deployments, custom settings, capacity discovery, quota, and region planning.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It prefers managed identity and project connections. Workflows that use environment files or API keys need careful redaction.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when those tools can access the skill files.
